Regulatory Engagement

• 

Serve as the primary point of contact with relevant regulatory bodies.

Ensure the organisation meets all applicable governance requirements, including fit and proper obligations for Approved and Designated Persons.

• 

Monitor and interpret regulatory developments relevant to virtual assets, and advise senior management and the Board accordingly.

Compliance Programme Development & Management

Design, implement, and maintain a comprehensive compliance framework aligned with local requirements, FATF recommendations, and international best practice for virtual asset service providers (VASPs).

Develop, review, and update all internal policies and procedures covering AML/CFT, KYC, customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, data protection, cybersecurity compliance, and safeguarding of client assets.

Establish and oversee the compliance monitoring programme, including periodic testing, gap analysis, and reporting to senior management and the Board.

Prepare and present regular compliance reports to the Board and relevant committees, including on regulatory changes, compliance breaches, and remediation progress.

Build and scale compliance policies governing advertising, social media campaigns, influencer partnerships, and product launches.

Partner with Legal, Product, and Marketing teams to operationalize a timely review process for client-facing assets and go-to-market materials.

• 

Act as the designated MLRO, with full statutory responsibility for overseeing the organisation's AML/CFT framework.

• 

Receive, review, and assess all internal Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from staff, and make informed decisions on whether to file external disclosures with competent local authorities.

Oversee and continuously improve the transaction monitoring programme, with support from global compliance and product functions.

• 

Ensure robust sanctions screening against all applicable lists, including OFAC, UK OFSI, UN, EU, and applicable local sanctions designations.

Oversee customer risk scoring, risk-based KYC/CDD processes, and enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers, politically exposed persons (PEPs), and customers from high-risk jurisdictions.

Act as a key member of the senior leadership team, providing compliance input on new products, services, partnerships, and business initiatives.

• 

Champion a strong compliance culture across the organisation through training, communications, and leadership by example.

• 

Ensure that the organisation's compliance obligations are adequately resourced, and advise the Board on staffing, systems, and budget requirements.

Establish and maintain a compliance manual, risk register and oversee the escalation and resolution of compliance incidents and breaches.

Prepare and submit all required regulatory reports and notifications to relevant authorities within stipulated deadlines.

Experience engaging directly with financial regulators and the financial intelligence unit

• 

Familiarity with the regional regulatory framework and requirements is strongly preferred.

Knowledge & Skills

Deep understanding of FATF Recommendations and their application to virtual asset service providers, including the Travel Rule (FATF Recommendation 16)

Strong knowledge of crypto-specific AML typologies.

ab5c729c552b8681.description: **About RentOk :** Running a PG or hostel in India means juggling rent, tenants, staff and complaints, mostly through a register, an Excel sheet, WhatsApp or a manager who remembers everything. RentOk brings all of it into one place. More than 25,000 property owners use it, from a 30-bed PG to co-living chains. Their tenants use it for their whole stay, from finding a place to moving out. We want RentOk to be intelligent, proactive and intuitive. It should fill in what it already knows instead of asking, suggest the next step, and do the work for the owner where it is safe. Owners already know the register. RentOk has to be easier than that, as well made as the best apps on their phone, and something people enjoy opening. RentOk is scaling, and we are growing our design team to match. With this role, design will be a team of three: two senior designers and a junior designer, working directly with our CPO. **The role: designer and builder :** Screens are cheap now. Anyone can generate ten in a minute. Choosing the right one, and knowing what to leave out, takes taste and judgment. And a designer no longer has to stop at a picture of the product. You can build the working thing. So we are hiring a product builder as much as a product designer. You will own whole parts of RentOk, like rent collection or a tenant's stay from booking to move-out, from the problem to the product in people's hands. You will know your part better than anyone: who uses it, why each feature exists, and what it does for the business. You will work with business, sales, support, marketing and operations, not only product and engineering, and help decide what we build next. Along the way you will grow our design system and hold the bar in design reviews. **What you will do :** * **Design workflows, not screens. A tenant moving out is one workflow:** the owner works out what the tenant still owes, the manager checks the room, the tenant waits for the deposit, and the parent who paid it wants to know when it comes back. Design all of it. * **Find the problem before you draw.** Visit properties, talk to owners, managers, staff and tenants, ask sharp questions, and turn an unclear problem into a clear direction. * **Make it intuitive for people who live on WhatsApp.** If a caretaker or a first-time owner needs help to use it, simplify until they don't. Write user-first UX copy yourself, in the words they use. * **Have a reason for every decision.** Bring options and a recommendation, and explain what you dropped and why. * **Build the working thing.** Take an idea to a working prototype with AI tools like Claude Code or Cursor, and test it with real users. * **Hand off without gaps.** Work with engineers from the start. Give them the rules, states, permissions, errors and messy real cases, like a partial payment or a tenant who leaves mid-month. If an engineer has to guess, the design is not finished. Then check the build before release, and check after release whether it worked. * **Put love into the details.** People can tell when someone cared. Type, spacing, motion and copy deserve the care the best consumer apps get, most of all where money moves. One wrong amount or a late deposit refund costs the owner the tenant's trust, and costs us the owner's. * **Decide when RentOk acts.** When it reminds, suggests or acts for the owner, when it stays quiet, and what happens when it gets something wrong. **Who we are looking for** * 2-3 years designing products, with shipped work and results you can show. * Taste and craft. You know what good looks like, you notice when something is off, and you can say why. * AI is part of how you design. You explore, prototype and test ideas with it. * Strong mobile app design on complex products: B2B, operations, fintech or marketplaces. * Clear communication. You can explain a decision to an engineer, a salesperson and a PG owner, in writing and in person. * Judgment. You hold a point of view, cut steps, and say no with reasons. **A plus if you have** * Shipped your own changes to a live product's code. * Designed products that move money. * Lived in a PG or hostel, or helped run one. **How to apply** Send two or three case studies showing the problem, your decisions and why, and what happened after launch. Include at least one workflow with more than one kind of user, and what you handed to engineers. If you have built something with AI, show us that too. To stand out, download [RentOk on the Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.eazypg.eazypgmanagerhttps://) or open [rentok.com](https://rentok.com/https://), pick one screen you would fix, and show us how.

Senior Network Developer
About Share
Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.
Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.
The Role
Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.
You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.
What you'll do
• 
Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.
• 
Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.
• 
Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.
• 
Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.
• 
Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.
• 
Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.
• 
Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.
• 
Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.
Our Ideal Candidate
• 
8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.
• 
Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.
• 
Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.
• 
Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.
• 
You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.
• 
You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.
• 
AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't.
• 
You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.
• 
A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.
Nice to have
• 
Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.
• 
Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them.
• 
Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.
• 
400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.
• 
Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.
• 
Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.
• 
DDoS mitigation at the edge.
If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)
